scope: Seventeen section29 research/provenance rows only. Primary public docs, exact remote repository source and installed package API inspection. No tracked file edits, provider account queries/mutations, purchases, sessions or load tests.

method.primarySources: Named vendor/institution/author/standards URLs were opened during this pass. Normative W3C screen-capture text supplements MDN. Only short paraphrases are retained; web cache publication/retrieval dates do not certify permanent source contents.
method.repository: Fresh read-only GitHub API main/contents calls resolved exact e9 source. Raw local Git blobs at that same SHA independently reproduce the retained package/lock/agent hashes. No repository content was mutated.
method.installedPackages: Existing installed package source was read only; no installation or provider connection was performed. Package version/API existence was checked against the exact repository lock. Package tarball integrities were not independently re-downloaded in this audit.
method.sourceSnapshotLimit: Full website/SDK artifacts and HTTP response headers are not archived. These observed claims need fresh verification if relied on after source drift.

rows.originalRequirement: Rechecked 9 September 2026. References support only the facts attributed to them. Owner requirements and proposed product defaults—overtime behavior, score aggregation, award definitions, audience separation, privacy/retention, tournament standings, and fault recovery—are not presented as universal debate rules. Source pages can change; match SDK documentation to installed versions.
supportedClaims: All seventeen reference/provenance rows were reviewed in this bounded pass. Technical documentation supports named provider/API facts only; the attached prompt separately supplies product defaults.
gaps: The scanned R3 mechanics were retrieved but not freshly visually inspected through the available screenshot output.
A comprehensive audit of every in-product/export provenance label was not performed.

rows.originalRequirement:
[R1] Casiciaco Recoletos Seminary, 6 April 2022: institutional account of a three-person Modified Oregon–Oxford event using 5/3/5 timing.
https://www.recoletosdebaguio.edu.ph/2022/04/06/cares-holds-philosophical-debate-during-jornadas-de-filosofia-2022/
supportedClaims: The seminary's account describes six participants in two three-person teams using Modified Oregon–Oxford 5/3/5 timing: five-minute speeches, three-minute interpellation and five-minute rebuttal.
gaps: This is an institution's event account, not a universal federation rule or application acceptance test.
rows.retrievalNote: Web retrieval initially exposed the page and then timed out on follow-up; a direct unauthenticated request to the same primary URL returned HTTP200 and the relevant article paragraph.

rows.originalRequirement:
[R2] Prof. Jensen DG. Mañebog, author-contributed tournament framework: full alternating sequence, preparation break and affirmative-last closing. It is an author's framework, not a national federation rulebook; its own case-label order and rubric differ from some other organizers.
https://ourhappyschool.com/debate/debate-tournament-framework-mechanics-guidelines-etc
supportedClaims: The page credits Jensen DG. Mañebog as preparer/contributor. It describes three-person teams, alternating 5/3 stages, a five-minute break, negative closing before affirmative closing, and its own 50/20/15/15 criteria.
gaps: Author-contributed framework only. Its case-label order and rubric must not be silently substituted for the owner's disclosed defaults.

rows.originalRequirement:
[R3] DENR Region V mechanics circulated by DepEd Catanduanes, 2023: PDF pages 5–7 visually inspected. Different timing, interpellation/moderator guidance, 25/30/30/15 weights, and listed awards. Its event's finality language is not a bar to this application's explicitly disclosed correction procedure. Do not copy apparent sequence typos from scans.
https://catanduanes.deped.gov.ph/files/UM---Inter-Schools-Debate-for-the-Environment-and-Battle-of-Best-Partnership-Initiatives-and-Awarding-Ceremonies.pdf
supportedClaims: The exact primary URL was accessible as a ten-page scanned PDF.
gaps: No text layer was returned. Screenshot requests for zero-based pages4/5/6 returned references but no model-visible image payload in this tool path; therefore timing, weights, listed awards and sequence typos were not independently visually rechecked.
The prompt's prior visual-inspection statement is preserved as supplied provenance, not adopted as this audit's observation.

rows.originalRequirement:
[T1] LiveKit background processor lifecycle and compatibility helpers.
https://github.com/livekit/track-processors-js/blob/main/processor-docs/video-processors.md
supportedClaims: Current vendor documentation exposes compatibility helpers and a disabled passthrough processor whose switchTo method changes effects while attachment is retained.
Installed package0.7.2 source contains disabled mode, switchTo, supportsBackgroundProcessors and supportsModernBackgroundProcessors, matching the exact repository lock.
gaps: Main-branch vendor docs are mutable. API existence does not prove leak-free lifecycle, moving remote video or physical-camera endurance.

rows.originalRequirement:
[T2] LiveKit signed access tokens, publish-source permissions, runtime updates, and Cloud vs self-hosted revocation behavior.
https://docs.livekit.io/frontends/reference/tokens-grants/
supportedClaims: LiveKit uses secret-signed JWT grants with independent camera, microphone, screen_share and screen_share_audio publish-source restrictions and runtime permission updates.

Current docs state automatic stale-token revocation on removal/permission changes is Cloud-only; self-hosted removal alone does not invalidate existing tokens. Token expiry controls initial connection, while connected clients receive refreshed tokens.
Installed server SDK2.18.0 exposes removeParticipant with revokeTokenTs, updateParticipant and canPublishSources.
gaps: The project's actual LiveKit deployment type, configured limits and real stale-role reconnect denial were not queried or exercised.

rows.originalRequirement:
[T3] LiveKit subscriptions, selective delivery, and adaptive stream.
https://docs.livekit.io/transport/media/subscribe/
supportedClaims: LiveKit documents selective subscription and track enable/disable controls. Adaptive stream selects layers from attached element size/visibility and pauses hidden tracks; JavaScript requires Track.attach for this behavior.
Installed client2.22.1 includes adaptive-stream handling and RemoteTrackPublication.setSubscribed.
gaps: Selective delivery is not an authorization boundary by itself. Actual subscriptions, private-room isolation and measured bandwidth/media quality still require live tests.

rows.originalRequirement:
[T4] LiveKit screen sharing and separate screen-share audio.
https://docs.livekit.io/transport/media/screenshare/
supportedClaims: Vendor docs show createScreenTracks with audio enabled and publishing each returned track. Screen-share audio has its own screen_share_audio publication, which must be received and played independently.
Installed client2.22.1 exposes createScreenTracks. The docs explicitly limit browser audio support and describe selecting a tab with audio consent.
gaps: No actual audio track, remote audibility, device consent or mobile publishing was tested. Screen video alone cannot close audio acceptance.

rows.originalRequirement:
[T5] Cloudflare Durable Objects: coordination and strongly consistent storage option, not a mandate to change the stack.
https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/
supportedClaims: Cloudflare documents named Durable Objects for coordination among clients and colocated transactional, strongly consistent storage.
gaps: This verifies an architectural option only; it does not require replacing the current transactional database or prove the application uses Durable Objects.

supportedClaims: Workers KV is eventually consistent; cross-location updates and previously cached negative lookups may remain stale for60 seconds or more. Cloudflare does not recommend it for atomic read/write transactions requiring stronger consistency.
gaps: This supports the persistence boundary, not a measurement of the actual application clock/state latency.

rows.originalRequirement:
[T7] LiveKit data transport; do not use room messages as the only persisted competition record.
https://docs.livekit.io/transport/data/packets/
supportedClaims: Reliable data packets are ordered and retransmitted on a best-effort basis; disconnected receivers can miss packets, and the server does not buffer them. Selective destination identities are supported.
gaps: Keeping official results in durable application storage is the architecture conclusion drawn from those limits; the vendor page is not evidence of this application's persistence or recovery correctness.

rows.originalRequirement:
[T8] MDN getDisplayMedia browser security/user-action requirements and compatibility.
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/MediaDevices/getDisplayMedia
supportedClaims: The normative Screen Capture API requires transient activation, a fully active/focused document and user selection; capture permission is not reusable as a persisted grant.
Audio is optional even when requested. MDN likewise documents per-browser/source variation and user-action requirements.
gaps: Current standards and documentation do not prove actual Chrome/Safari/mobile behavior, renewed consent, supported audio sources or this application's handling.

rows.originalRequirement:
[T9] W3C accessibility guidance for pointer target size. The 44-pixel main-control preference in this prompt is a product choice, not a misstatement of the 24-pixel WCAG 2.2 minimum criterion and its exceptions.
https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html
supportedClaims: WCAG2.2 criterion2.5.8 specifies24 by24 CSS pixels with spacing, equivalent-control, inline, user-agent-control and essential exceptions. The prompt's44-pixel main-control preference is a stricter product choice.
gaps: No application-wide target geometry, keyboard, screen-reader, zoom or accessibility conformance audit was performed.

rows.originalRequirement:
[T10] Supabase row-level authorization and service-key bypass considerations.
https://supabase.com/features/row-level-security
supportedClaims: Supabase documents database-level row authorization and separate grant/policy checks. Server secret/service_role access can bypass RLS and must not be exposed in a browser.
The detailed docs qualify that a request carrying a user's access token uses that user's RLS context even if its client was initialized with a secret key.
gaps: Documentation does not prove the actual Worker authorizes every privileged path; existing scoped database/security receipts remain separate evidence.

rows.originalRequirement:
[T11] LiveKit project-level quotas, participant-minutes and transfer metering. Verify actual account allowances before using any displayed number as deployment capacity.
https://docs.livekit.io/deploy/admin/quotas-and-limits/
supportedClaims: Current public documentation lists Build defaults of100 project-wide connected participants,5000 monthly WebRTC participant-minutes and50GB downstream transfer. It also lists100 video and100 audio subscriptions per active participant.
The provider directs operators to the project's dashboard settings for actual limits. Participant-minutes measure connected-user time; transfer includes media and data.
gaps: Actual project plan, remaining allowance, Study Room commitments, reconnect/private-room headroom, approved spending and10/25/50/100 ramp remain unverified. Published defaults must not be presented as available capacity.

limits: A research-only fact becoming eligible for ledger review does not promote the entire row or any acceptance clause automatically. The parent must reconcile existing coverage and retain outstanding runtime/device/account gates.
The original prompt identifies owner defaults separately from cited tournament frameworks; no universal national rules, certification, legal authority or third-party endorsement is established.
The R3 scanned PDF was retrieved but current visual verification was not possible through the available tool output, so no fresh claim about its scanned weights/timings/awards is made.

Actual LiveKit plan/usage/deployment type, runtime permission revocation, real audio/video/share audio, physical device matrix, approved ramp, real mail and at-least90-minute physical endurance remain open.
